newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sacks controversial senior official.
newsitem.headline: France sacks controversial senior official.

text.p: The French cabinet sacked a controversial senior official from his post as prefect (chief administrator) of the Var department of southern France on Wednesday, appointing him to a job with little real responsibility.

Jean-Charles Marchiani, known for hard-right views, had been at the centre of several political rows in recent months and his demotion was widely expected after a Socialist-led cabinet took over following last month's general election.

Marchiani, 53, who had held the Var job since 1995, was appointed secretary-general of the Paris defence zone, a civil defence post which would only take on real responsibilities in the event the French capital came under air attack or similar threat.

Marchiani's long career had until 1995 been mostly on the fringes of the secret services and his speciality had been in negotiating with clandestine groups in Bosnia or Lebanon where he secured the release of French hostages held by Iranian-backed Lebanese guerrillas in Beirut in the 1980s.
He was accused of being overly friendly with the extreme rightist mayor of Toulon, the Var's main city, and making outspoken statements which embarassed even the previous centre-right cabinet.
As prefect, Marchiani had been expected to stay aloof from party politics but he regularly made enemies across the spectrum by his public stances.

Marchiani raised eyebrows in officially secular France last year when he said his "Christian convictions" led him to take action against a popular rap group in trouble with authorities for lyrics allegedly inciting attacks against the police.
He also sought to withdraw public subsidies to a respected theatre festival because he thought it was overly friendly to leftist themes.
